examples.ko: 저는 이번 달부터 병원에서 견습을 시작했어요.
examples.en: I started my apprenticeship at a hospital this month.
The pay is a bit lower during the training period.

examples.ko: 지금은 견습 중이라 모르는 게 많아요.
examples.en: I'm still in training, so there's a lot I don't know.

examples.ko: 견습이 끝나면 정식 직원이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: When the apprenticeship ends, you can become a regular employee.
He learned the work as an apprentice at a hair salon.
She started as a trainee and is now a team leader.

explain: 직업을 배우는 중인 사람이나 그 기간에 쓰는 말이에요. '견습 사원', '견습 기간'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙는 일이 많아요. '수습'과 비슷한 자리에서 쓰지만, '견습'은 보고 배운다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who is learning a trade, or to that period. It often comes before other words, as in '견습 사원' and '견습 기간'. It is used in similar places as '수습', but '견습' has a stronger feel of learning by watching.

examples.en: He was hired by a small restaurant.
I was hired by a new company last month.
The people who were hired start work tomorrow.
When you are hired as an employee, you sign a contract.
Ten people in total will be hired.
I am hired only three days a week.

explain: '취직하다'는 내가 일자리를 얻었다는 느낌이고, '고용되다'는 회사가 나를 쓰기로 했다는 쪽에서 말해요. 보통 '식당에 고용되다'처럼 '에'를 써요. 회사 쪽은 '고용하다'예요.
explain_en: '취직하다' says that I got a job, while '고용되다' describes it from the side of the company choosing to use me. It usually takes '에', as in '식당에 고용되다'. The company side uses '고용하다'.

examples.en: The new employee is being assigned to the sales team.
The desks are arranged by the window.
Police were stationed all over the place.

examples.ko: 다음 달부터 지방 지사로 배치될 거예요.
examples.en: I will be posted to a regional branch starting next month.

examples.ko: 가구가 잘 배치된 방은 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: A room with well-arranged furniture looks spacious.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 여러 부서에 나뉘어 배치되고 있어요.
examples.en: The new hires are being split up and assigned to several departments.

explain: 사람은 '부서에 배치되다'처럼 일할 자리에 정해지고, 물건은 '가구가 배치되다'처럼 자리를 잡아요. 같은 뜻의 능동형은 '배치하다'이고, 회사에서는 '발령'이라는 말도 같이 써요. 보통 '~에 배치되다'로 장소나 부서가 꼭 따라와요.
explain_en: For people it means being assigned to a post, as in '부서에 배치되다'; for objects it means being set in a place, like furniture. The active form is 배치하다, and at companies 발령 is also used. It almost always comes with a place or department: '~에 배치되다'.

examples.en: The family has been moving around busily since morning.

examples.ko: 직원들이 손님 맞을 준비로 분주히 일해요.
examples.en: The staff are busily working to get ready for the guests.
People in the market come and go busily.

examples.ko: 그는 발표 준비를 하느라 분주히 뛰어다녔어요.
examples.en: He ran around busily preparing for the presentation.

examples.ko: 명절 전날 부엌에서는 모두 분주히 음식을 만들어요.
examples.en: The day before the holiday, everyone in the kitchen is busily cooking.
People are walking hurriedly through the airport.

explain: '바쁘게'보다 이리저리 서두르며 움직이는 모습이 잘 보일 때 써요. 보통 '분주히 움직이다', '분주히 오가다'처럼 몸이 움직이는 말과 같이 나와요. 형용사는 '분주하다'예요.
explain_en: Compared with '바쁘게', it fits when you can picture people hurrying around here and there. It usually pairs with words of movement, as in '분주히 움직이다' or '분주히 오가다'. The adjective is '분주하다'.

en: be piled; be heaped; be accumulated

examples.ko: 해야 할 숙제가 산적해 있어서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I am worried because I have a pile of homework to do.

examples.ko: 새 정부 앞에는 해결할 문제가 산적해요.
examples.en: The new government has a pile of problems to solve.

examples.ko: 산적한 업무를 하루 만에 끝내기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to finish the piled-up work in one day.

examples.ko: 회사에 과제가 산적했지만 팀원들이 힘을 모았어요.
examples.en: The company had many tasks piled up, but the team pulled together.

examples.ko: 문제가 산적할수록 차분하게 순서를 정해야 해요.
examples.en: The more problems pile up, the more calmly you need to set an order.

examples.ko: 연휴가 끝나면 처리할 메일이 산적해 있을 것 같아요.
examples.en: After the holiday, I think there will be a pile of emails to handle.

explain: 일, 문제, 과제처럼 해결할 것이 많이 쌓였을 때 써요. 물건이 쌓인 모습은 보통 '쌓이다'라고 하고, '현안이 산적해 있다'처럼 주로 '산적해 있다' 꼴로 뉴스에 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when many things to deal with, like work, problems or tasks, have built up. For stacked objects people usually say '쌓이다', and it often appears in the news as '산적해 있다', as in '현안이 산적해 있다'.

examples.ko: 이 수업은 실무적인 내용을 많이 가르쳐요.
examples.en: This class teaches a lot of practical, work-related content.

examples.ko: 회사에서는 실무적으로 도움이 되는 경험이 중요해요.
examples.en: At a company, experience that helps in practical work matters.

examples.ko: 그 일은 실무적 지식이 없으면 하기 어려워요.
examples.en: That job is hard to do without hands-on working knowledge.
I was glad to be rated as practical-minded in the interview.
I know the theory, but I'm not hands-on, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 실무적이어서 설명도 아주 구체적이에요.
examples.en: Our team leader is hands-on, so the explanations are very concrete.

explain: '이론적'과 달리 실제로 일을 하는 현장과 관련될 때 써요. '실무 경험', '실무자'처럼 '실무'와 함께 외워 두면 좋아요. 회사 이야기나 취업 준비에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: In contrast to '이론적' (theoretical), it relates to actual work on the job. It is useful to learn it with '실무 경험' and '실무자'. You hear it in talk about companies and job hunting.

examples.ko: 이 동네로 전입한 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since I moved into this neighborhood.
When you move, you have to register at your new address.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 학교로 전입한 학생이 열 명이에요.
examples.en: Ten students transferred into our school this year.

examples.ko: 지난달에 다른 구청에서 우리 구청으로 전입했어요.
examples.en: Last month I transferred to our district office from another one.

examples.ko: 다른 도시에서 전입하는 사람이 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of people moving in from other cities keeps growing.

examples.ko: 언제 전입했는지 주민등록 서류에 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The residence registration documents show when you moved in.

explain: 반의어는 '전출하다'예요. 이사는 '이사하다'가 일상적이고, '전입하다'는 주소를 옮겨 등록하거나 학교·부서로 옮겨 올 때처럼 공식적인 상황에서 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '전출하다'. In daily life '이사하다' is the usual word for moving, while '전입하다' is used in official situations such as registering a new address or transferring into a school or department.

examples.en: The boss gives instructions to the staff.
The teacher told us to do the homework first.
The doctor instructed me to take the medicine.
Is it okay if I do it as you instructed?
The team leader speaks clearly when giving instructions.
Don't do anything I haven't instructed.

explain: 회사나 학교에서 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 할 일을 정해 줄 때 써요. 친구에게 부탁할 때는 쓰지 않아요. '시키다'는 일상에서 더 가볍게 써요.
explain_en: Used when a superior assigns work to someone below at a company or school. You do not use it when asking a friend. '시키다' is a lighter everyday alternative.

examples.en: I commute by subway.

examples.ko: 매일 한 시간씩 통근하는 게 힘들어요.
examples.en: Commuting an hour every day is hard.
The office was far, so I commuted by bus.

examples.ko: 회사 가까이로 이사하면 통근할 때 편해요.
examples.en: If you move closer to your workplace, commuting is easier.
I used to commute by car, but now I go by bicycle.
I commute from Seoul to Incheon.

explain: 출근은 일하러 가는 것, 퇴근은 일을 마치고 가는 것, 통근은 집과 직장을 오가는 것 전체예요. 말할 때는 '출근해요'를 더 많이 쓰고 통근하다는 글과 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 회사 버스는 '통근 버스'라고 해요.
explain_en: 출근 is going to work, 퇴근 is leaving after work, and 통근 is the whole trip between home and work. In speech 출근해요 is more common, while 통근하다 appears often in writing and news. A company shuttle is a 통근 버스.

en: be put in; be thrown in; be deployed

examples.en: The rescue team was sent to the scene right away.
A new player comes on in the second half.
A lot of money was put into this project.

examples.ko: 신입 직원이 팀에 투입되면 먼저 교육을 받아요.
examples.en: When a new employee joins a team, they get training first.

examples.ko: 투입된 인원이 너무 적어서 일이 느려요.
examples.en: The work is slow because too few people were assigned.
The order in which materials are put in matters.

explain: 투입하다의 피동이에요. 사람이 어떤 자리에 보내질 때는 '현장에 투입되다'라고 해요. 스포츠에서 교체 선수가 경기에 나가는 것도 투입이에요. '돈이 투입되다'처럼 물건과 돈도 주어가 돼요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '투입하다'. When a person is sent to a post, we say '현장에 투입되다'. A substitute going onto the field in sports is also 투입. Money and materials can be the subject too, as in '돈이 투입되다'.
